key_test: aov(PD ~ HiLoCat * Task + Error(ID/Task)) on repdatalong.csv (3 rows per ID: Weapons-Black, Weapons-White, Flankers); key effect HiLoCat:Task in the ID:Task stratum
exclusions: none; all 75 IDs in the derived PD file

r_script.es: not printed by the script (assignment only); from its printed SS 0.01014/(0.01014+1.7115) = 0.0059
r_script.how: audit script run unmodified through a shim that maps getOSFfile() to the local downloaded copy and skips library(httr), library(RCurl) and the remote source() of getOSFfile.R (no network beyond osf.io)

agreement: all three agree (F 0.432, p .513, partial eta^2 .006); every stratum of the Python projection fit matches R's summary (HiLoCat F 1.454 p .232; Task F .505 p .480)
notes: n_after_exclusions counts rows; 75 participants. The survey's worry that the duplicated Weapons rows make a 'cleaner' analysis differ does not hold for the interaction: averaging the two Weapons rows per ID gives the identical F(1,73) = 0.4323, p = .5129, because the ID:Task stratum already contrasts Flankers with the Weapons mean. The authors' own analysis file fits the same aov. PD scores are derived; rebuilding them from trials needs a helper script not on OSF, so this reproduces the test, not the scoring.
